overview: The National Resource Efficiency Policy (NREP) is a policy framework aimed at promoting resource efficiency and circular economy principles across sectors in India. It seeks to reduce environmental impact through sustainable resource use, waste minimization, and recycling initiatives. The policy is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and aligns with national goals for sustainable development and climate resilience.
objectives: Promote resource efficiency across all sectors of the economy
Reduce waste generation and enhance recycling and reuse
Support circular economy business models and innovation
Strengthen policy and regulatory frameworks for sustainable resource management
Enhance capacity building and awareness on resource efficiency
Encourage adoption of eco-friendly technologies and practices
Monitor and evaluate resource use efficiency through measurable indicators
eligibility: The policy applies to all sectors including industries, MSMEs, startups, research institutions, and local governments engaged in activities related to resource use, waste management, and sustainable production. Specific eligibility for support under NREP-linked initiatives may vary based on the implementing agency and program guidelines.
benefits: Benefits include access to technical guidance, policy support, potential financial incentives under linked schemes, capacity building programs, and recognition for adopting resource-efficient practices. It also facilitates access to national and international best practices in circular economy and sustainable resource management.
financial_support: Financial support under NREP is channeled through allied government schemes and programs such as the Fund of Funds for Startups, MSME credit guarantee schemes, and environmental protection funds. The policy itself does not allocate direct financial aid but enables convergence with existing financial instruments for green innovation and waste valorization.
application_process: 1. Identify relevant NREP-aligned schemes or programs under MoEFCC or partner ministries. 2. Check eligibility criteria for the specific scheme (e.g., startup, MSME, or industrial upgrade). 3. Prepare required documents including project proposal, incorporation certificates, and technical details. 4. Apply through the designated portal or nodal agency. 5. Submit application and await evaluation. 6. If approved, receive sanction and implement the project as per guidelines.
required_documents: Project proposal detailing resource efficiency measures
PAN and GST details of the entity
Undertaking on compliance with environmental norms
deadlines: Varies by scheme; generally rolling basis or as per specific program notifications
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
caveats: NREP is a policy framework and not a direct funding scheme; benefits are accessed through linked programs
Financial and technical support depends on alignment with specific scheme guidelines
Implementation and monitoring are subject to periodic review by MoEFCC
Benefits may be limited to pilot or scale-up phases based on available budget
